## Summary

Follow up to #5467 (review point 2 there). The facade recorded backend import errors per attn_gym module, but every placeholder raised the first recorded error, so with, say, `attn_gym.sparse` failing on cutlass and the GDN modules importing fine, `GDNKernel.Config().build()` reported cutlass although GDN would have worked.

- Exports of a module whose backend is missing now resolve to a `_MissingKernel` subclass carrying that module's error (one subclass per module, cached, named `_MissingKernel[<attn_gym module>]`). Calling it, `.apply`, or `.from_fragments` raises a fresh `ModuleNotFoundError` with that backend's name and message.
- `is_missing_kernel()` (a `TypeGuard`) replaces the `is not _MissingKernel` identity checks in `kda.py`, `gdn.py`, `linear_attention.py` and `cp_linear_attention.py`, so the subclasses are also kept out of SPMD registration.
- `require_attn_gym(kernel, *kernels)` checks the given exports and each module calls it from `__init__` with every export it uses, so a build error names the backend that module needs: `KDAKernel` (`chunk_kda`, `bound_gate`, `l2norm`), `GDNKernel` (`chunk_gdn`, `recurrent_gdn`, `l2norm`), `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN` (`causal_conv1d`), `ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` (`context_parallel_kda` / `context_parallel_gdn`, `context_parallel_conv_history`, `ContextParallelRouting`, and `l2norm` for GDN). The zero argument form from #5467, which raised on any error recorded so far, is gone.
- No change when `attn_gym` is missing (the placeholders are the base class and raise the install hint) or when every backend imports.

Not in this PR: attn_gym resolves `causal_conv1d` and the other `attn_gym.linear.short_conv` exports lazily (`attn_gym.linear._lazy`) and raises a plain `ImportError` at attribute access, which `_load_module` never sees, so on a machine without cutlass `gdn.py` / `kda.py` still fail to import and 18 CPU test modules do not collect. I have that fixed on top of this branch and will open it next, the `causal_conv1d` checks here are what make it fail at build rather than at the first forward.

## Test plan

`tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_optional_imports.py`:
- new `test_attention_modules_report_their_own_backend_at_build`: a fake attn_gym whose modules all import except the broken ones. With `attn_gym.linear.short_conv` failing on cutlass, `KDAKernel` / `GDNKernel` build and `InnerKDA`, `InnerGDN` and their CP variants fail at build with cutlass, with the three context parallel modules failing on triton, the inner modules build and the CP variants fail with triton. Fails without the `__init__` checks.
- mixed case extended: `…l2norm_fwd` fails on triton and `attn_gym.linear.kda.impl.fused` on cutlass in one process, `_L2Norm()` raises triton, `_ChunkKDA()` / `.apply` raise cutlass, `require_attn_gym(_ChunkKDA)` raises cutlass, `require_attn_gym(real, _L2Norm)` raises triton, `require_attn_gym(real, real)` passes, the placeholder is named after its module.
- broken backend case asserts the placeholders are subclasses and that none reached the SPMD registry.
- existing `[cutlass-*]` build cases now go through `require_attn_gym(kernels)` and still see `error.name == "cutlass"`.

On macOS without cutlass/triton, rebased on e61df55, 15 passed, `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/checkpointer` 123 passed (2 known, meta-pytorch/torch_checkpointing#9), pre commit on all files passes every hook except pyrefly, which reports the same pre existing diagnostics as main in files this PR does not touch.

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 1m 25s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/39166168965)

---
### Review: per-kernel backend errors for the attn_gym facade

The change is correct and fixes the problem it targets: when one attn_gym module fails on a backend, that failure no longer blocks kernels from other modules. Turning placeholders into per-module subclasses, cached in `_BACKEND_KERNELS`, is a small and clean way to do it. Switching to `is_missing_kernel()` everywhere also keeps the subclasses out of SPMD registration. I checked the whole repo outside `tests/` and no `is _MissingKernel` identity checks are left. My comments are below, most important first.

#### 1. The narrower build check lets CP backend failures through until `forward` (worth deciding on purpose)
`ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` build `KDAKernel` / `GDNKernel` through `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN`. Those now check only `chunk_kda, bound_gate, l2norm` or `chunk_gdn, recurrent_gdn, l2norm`. Their own kernels are not checked:
- `context_parallel_kda` / `context_parallel_gdn`
- `context_parallel_conv_history` and `ContextParallelRouting` (`attn_gym.linear.context_parallel`)
- the short-conv exports

Before this PR, importing `cp_kda.py` touched `context_parallel_kda` at import time. So a backend failure there was recorded, and the old coarse `require_attn_gym()` raised at **build**. Now the build succeeds and the error only appears at the first `forward`, after model init, sharding and possibly checkpoint load. The error message is still correct; it just shows up later.

Suggestion: have each CP inner module call `require_attn_gym(context_parallel_kda, context_parallel_conv_history, ContextParallelRouting)` in its `__init__` (same for GDN). Then the "fails at build" contract holds for CP too. If late failure on CP is acceptable, add a sentence to the PR description saying so.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20attn-gym-per-kernel-errors%2C%20add%20require_attn_gym(context_parallel_kda%2C%20context_parallel_conv_history%2C%20ContextParallelRouting)%20to%20ContextParallelInnerKDA.__init__%20in%20torchtitan%2Fmodels%2Fcommon%2Fattention%2Fcp_kda.py%20and%20the%20GDN%20equivalent%20in%20cp_gdn.py%20so%20CP%20backend%20failures%20surface%20at%20build%20time%2C%20and%20extend%20test_optional_imports.py%20accordingly.&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)

#### 2. Kernel lists are copied by hand from `forward`
`attention/kda.py:74` and `attention/gdn.py:223` restate which exports `forward` / `prepare_inputs` / `_recurrent_gdn_fwd` call. If someone adds a kernel call and forgets to update the list, nothing fails; the build check just gets weaker. I don't see an easy way to enforce this mechanically. At minimum, a short comment at each `require_attn_gym(...)` call ("must list every attn_gym export used by forward") would help reviewers catch drift.

#### 3. Calling with zero arguments silently switches to the coarse check
`require_attn_gym(*kernels)` with no arguments means "fail if anything recorded so far failed", which is a different and stricter check. A caller passing an empty, computed tuple would get it without noticing. No production callers use the zero-argument form any more; only the test at `test_optional_imports.py:299/441` does. Per CLAUDE.md's "no speculative" guidance, consider dropping the coarse branch and keeping one meaning. If it stays, the docstring should state the split more directly.

#### 4. `TypeGuard` would remove the `cast` (nit)
```python
from typing import TypeGuard

def is_missing_kernel(kernel: object) -> TypeGuard[type[_MissingKernel]]:
    return isinstance(kernel, type) and issubclass(kernel, _MissingKernel)
```
Then `require_attn_gym` can use `kernel._error` directly, and the `cast` import goes away.

#### 5. Every subclass has the same name (nit)
`type("_MissingKernel", ...)` gives each per-module subclass the same `__name__` / `__qualname__` as the base, so reprs and tracebacks can't tell them apart. Something like `f"_MissingKernel[{module_name}]"`, or a name that includes `error.name`, would make debugging easier. It costs nothing, since identity checks are gone.

#### 6. Small points (fine as they are)
- `_raise_for(None)` falling back to "first recorded backend error" is now only reachable through the zero-argument `require_attn_gym()`. The base `_MissingKernel` is only handed out when `attn_gym` is absent, and in that case `_BACKEND_ERRORS` is empty. If you drop the coarse branch (#3), this fallback can go too.
- `_BACKEND_ERRORS.setdefault` combined with the cached subclass means a second export from the same failed module reuses the first error. That is the correct behaviour.
- The tests are thorough. The mixed triton/cutlass case in a single process covers the original bug directly.

### Not verified
I couldn't run `pytest` here because the command needed permission this job doesn't have. The review is based on reading the code only.

- [x] Read the PR diff and the full `attn_gym.py`
- [x] Audited callsites (`kda`, `gdn`, `linear_attention`, `cp_linear_attention`, `cp_kda`, `cp_gdn`, tests)
- [x] Posted review

> @mkhilari could you address comments

Thanks @tianyu-l for the review. Pushed a follow up commit addressing it:

1. `ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` now check the exports they call in `__init__` (`context_parallel_kda` / `context_parallel_gdn`, `context_parallel_conv_history`, `ContextParallelRouting`, plus `l2norm` for GDN), and `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN` check `causal_conv1d`, so every module keeps the fails at build contract. New `test_attention_modules_report_their_own_backend_at_build` covers both directions, with the CP modules broken the inner modules build and the CP ones fail with the CP backend, with `short_conv` broken the kernels build and the inner modules fail. It fails on the previous revision. `InnerGDN` only needs `causal_conv1d` on its packed sequence and CP paths (the no cu_seqlens path is pure torch), I kept one rule, check every export the module can call, rather than special casing that path, happy to narrow it if you prefer. The `causal_conv1d` checks only bite once the lazy export follow up lands, today a missing cutlass fails at import of `kda.py` / `gdn.py`, as the description notes.
2. Every `require_attn_gym` call has a keep in sync comment.
3. Dropped the zero argument form, `require_attn_gym(kernel, *kernels)`. The first recorded error fallback in `_raise_for` went with it (your point 6).
4. `is_missing_kernel` returns `TypeGuard[type[_MissingKernel]]`, no cast.
5. Placeholder subclasses are named `_MissingKernel[<attn_gym module>]`.

Verified on macOS without cutlass/triton, `test_optional_imports.py` 15 passed, pre commit passes every hook except pyrefly, which reports the same pre existing diagnostics as main in files this PR does not touch.

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 1m 38s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/39181091200)

---
### Re-review after f51e271

I have no blocking comments. All five points from the first review are addressed, and the new commit reads cleanly.

- [x] Read the diff (`e61df55..HEAD`)
- [x] Check how the earlier review points were addressed
- [x] Look for new issues
- [x] Post the review

#### Earlier points
| # | Point | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CP failures surfaced only at `forward` | ✅ `ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` check their exports in `__init__`, and `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN` check `causal_conv1d`. MRO is fine: `CPInnerAttention` has no `__init__`, so `super().__init__(config)` reaches `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN.__init__`, which then builds the kernel. All three layers are checked, outermost first. |
| 2 | Kernel lists can drift from `forward` | ✅ Each call has a keep-in-sync comment |
| 3 | Zero-argument coarse form | ✅ Removed. The signature `require_attn_gym(kernel, *kernels)` makes an empty call a `TypeError` |
| 4 | `TypeGuard` | ✅ No `cast` remains |
| 5 | Placeholder names | ✅ Placeholders are named `_MissingKernel[<module>]` |

#### Checks on the lists against actual call sites
- `KDAKernel`: `chunk_kda` (forward), plus `bound_gate` and `l2norm` (`prepare_inputs`). Complete.
- `GDNKernel`: `chunk_gdn` and `l2norm` (forward), and `recurrent_gdn` (inside `_recurrent_gdn_fwd`). Complete.
- `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN`: `causal_conv1d`, also reached through `_causal_conv1d_varlen`. Complete. Applying the rule uniformly, including the pure-torch no-`cu_seqlens` path in GDN, seems right to me. A model that can only build in some layouts would be surprising.
- `ContextParallelInnerKDA`: `context_parallel_conv_history` (`short_convolution`), `context_parallel_kda` (`kda_core`), and `ContextParallelRouting` (via `prepare_linear_attention_cp_metadata`, which calls `ContextParallelRouting.from_fragments`). Complete.
- `ContextParallelInnerGDN`: the same exports plus `l2norm` in `gdn_core`. Complete.
- When `attn_gym` is not installed, the old `_load_module("attn_gym") is None` branch is no longer needed. Every export then resolves to the base `_MissingKernel` with `_error = None`, so `require_attn_gym` still raises the install hint.
- No `is _MissingKernel` / `is not _MissingKernel` identity checks remain outside tests.

#### Remaining nits (optional)
1. **The CP case in the new test can't catch a dropped export.** In the `context_parallel` parametrization, all three CP modules fail with the same backend (`triton`). Removing, say, `context_parallel_conv_history` or `ContextParallelRouting` from the `cp_kda.py` list would still pass, because `context_parallel_kda` raises `triton` first. To make each entry load-bearing, break one module per case and give each its own backend name. For example: `attn_gym.linear.context_parallel` → `"backend_a"` should fail both CP modules, and `attn_gym.linear.kda.context_parallel` → `"backend_b"` should fail only `cp_inner_kda`. This is the test-side half of point 2: the comment documents the contract, and this would enforce it.
   [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20attn-gym-per-kernel-errors%2C%20in%20tests%2Funit_tests%2Fcpu%2Fmodels%2Fcommon%2Ftest_optional_imports.py%20test_attention_modules_report_their_own_backend_at_build%2C%20split%20the%20context_parallel%20parametrization%20so%20each%20of%20attn_gym.linear.context_parallel%2C%20attn_gym.linear.kda.context_parallel%20and%20attn_gym.linear.gdn.context_parallel%20is%20broken%20on%20its%20own%20(with%20a%20distinct%20backend%20name)%2C%20asserting%20exactly%20which%20of%20cp_inner_kda%20%2F%20cp_inner_gdn%20fail%20with%20that%20backend%20and%20that%20the%20others%20build.&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)
2. **The vLLM inner modules still fail late (out of scope, pre-existing).** `VLLMInnerKDA` and `VLLMInnerGDN` (`torchtitan/rl/generator/vllm/{kda,gdn}.py`) call `paged_chunk_kda`, `paged_causal_conv1d`, `causal_conv1d_decode`, `recurrent_*_decode`, `l2norm` and `bound_gate`, but never call `require_attn_gym`. A missing backend therefore only shows up at the first generator step. They never had the check, so this PR doesn't regress them. It could go into the lazy-`short_conv` follow-up if you want the build-time guarantee to cover the generator too.

### Not verified
I couldn't run `pytest`, because this job doesn't have permission for that command. This review is based on reading the code only.

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "broken_modules, missing_backend",
+    [
+        (("attn_gym.linear.short_conv",), "cutlass"),
+        (
+            (
+                "attn_gym.linear.context_parallel",
+                "attn_gym.linear.gdn.context_parallel",
+                "attn_gym.linear.kda.context_parallel",
+            ),
+            "triton",
+        ),
+    ],
+    ids=["short_conv", "context_parallel"],
+)
+def test_attention_modules_report_their_own_backend_at_build(
+    broken_modules: tuple[str, ...], missing_backend: str
+) -> None:
+    """A module fails at build when an export it calls lacks its backend."""
+    script = r"""
+import importlib.abc
+import importlib.util
+import sys
+
+broken_modules = sys.argv[1].split(",")
+missing_backend = sys.argv[2]
+
+
+class FakeAttentionGym(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder, importlib.abc.Loader):
+    # Every attn_gym module imports and exports a class under any name, except
+    # the broken ones, whose backend is missing.
+
+    def find_spec(self, fullname, path, target=None):
+        if fullname in broken_modules:
+            raise ModuleNotFoundError("blocked dependency", name=missing_backend)
+        if fullname == "attn_gym" or fullname.startswith("attn_gym."):
+            return importlib.util.spec_from_loader(fullname, self, is_package=True)
+        return None
+
+    def create_module(self, spec):
+        return None
+
+    def exec_module(self, module):
+        def export(name):
+            if name.startswith("__"):
+                raise AttributeError(name)
+            return type(name, (), {})
+
+        module.__getattr__ = export
+
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, FakeAttentionGym())
+
+from torchtitan.models.common.attention import cp_gdn, cp_kda, gdn, kda
+from torchtitan.models.common.attn_gym import is_missing_kernel
+
+kda_kernel = kda.KDAKernel.Config()
+gdn_kernel = gdn.GDNKernel.Config()
+inner_kda = kda.InnerKDA.Config(head_dim=128, conv_kernel_size=4, kernel=kda_kernel)
+inner_gdn = gdn.InnerGDN.Config(conv_kernel_size=4, kernel=gdn_kernel)
+cp_inner_kda = cp_kda.ContextParallelInnerKDA.Config(
+    head_dim=128, conv_kernel_size=4, kernel=kda_kernel
+)
+cp_inner_gdn = cp_gdn.ContextParallelInnerGDN.Config(
+    conv_kernel_size=4, kernel=gdn_kernel
+)
+
+
+def backend_of(config):
+    try:
+        config.build()
+    except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
+        assert str(error) == "blocked dependency", error
+        return error.name
+    return None
+
+
+# The kernels' own exports imported, so they build whichever module is broken.
+assert backend_of(kda_kernel) is None

---
### Review: per-kernel backend errors for the attn_gym facade

The change is correct and fixes the problem it targets: when one attn_gym module fails on a backend, that failure no longer blocks kernels from other modules. Turning placeholders into per-module subclasses, cached in `_BACKEND_KERNELS`, is a small and clean way to do it. Switching to `is_missing_kernel()` everywhere also keeps the subclasses out of SPMD registration. I checked the whole repo outside `tests/` and no `is _MissingKernel` identity checks are left. My comments are below, most important first.

#### 1. The narrower build check lets CP backend failures through until `forward` (worth deciding on purpose)
`ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` build `KDAKernel` / `GDNKernel` through `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN`. Those now check only `chunk_kda, bound_gate, l2norm` or `chunk_gdn, recurrent_gdn, l2norm`. Their own kernels are not checked:
- `context_parallel_kda` / `context_parallel_gdn`
- `context_parallel_conv_history` and `ContextParallelRouting` (`attn_gym.linear.context_parallel`)
- the short-conv exports

Before this PR, importing `cp_kda.py` touched `context_parallel_kda` at import time. So a backend failure there was recorded, and the old coarse `require_attn_gym()` raised at **build**. Now the build succeeds and the error only appears at the first `forward`, after model init, sharding and possibly checkpoint load. The error message is still correct; it just shows up later.

Suggestion: have each CP inner module call `require_attn_gym(context_parallel_kda, context_parallel_conv_history, ContextParallelRouting)` in its `__init__` (same for GDN). Then the "fails at build" contract holds for CP too. If late failure on CP is acceptable, add a sentence to the PR description saying so.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20attn-gym-per-kernel-errors%2C%20add%20require_attn_gym(context_parallel_kda%2C%20context_parallel_conv_history%2C%20ContextParallelRouting)%20to%20ContextParallelInnerKDA.__init__%20in%20torchtitan%2Fmodels%2Fcommon%2Fattention%2Fcp_kda.py%20and%20the%20GDN%20equivalent%20in%20cp_gdn.py%20so%20CP%20backend%20failures%20surface%20at%20build%20time%2C%20and%20extend%20test_optional_imports.py%20accordingly.&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)

#### 2. Kernel lists are copied by hand from `forward`
`attention/kda.py:74` and `attention/gdn.py:223` restate which exports `forward` / `prepare_inputs` / `_recurrent_gdn_fwd` call. If someone adds a kernel call and forgets to update the list, nothing fails; the build check just gets weaker. I don't see an easy way to enforce this mechanically. At minimum, a short comment at each `require_attn_gym(...)` call ("must list every attn_gym export used by forward") would help reviewers catch drift.

#### 3. Calling with zero arguments silently switches to the coarse check
`require_attn_gym(*kernels)` with no arguments means "fail if anything recorded so far failed", which is a different and stricter check. A caller passing an empty, computed tuple would get it without noticing. No production callers use the zero-argument form any more; only the test at `test_optional_imports.py:299/441` does. Per CLAUDE.md's "no speculative" guidance, consider dropping the coarse branch and keeping one meaning. If it stays, the docstring should state the split more directly.

#### 4. `TypeGuard` would remove the `cast` (nit)
```python
from typing import TypeGuard

def is_missing_kernel(kernel: object) -> TypeGuard[type[_MissingKernel]]:
    return isinstance(kernel, type) and issubclass(kernel, _MissingKernel)
```
Then `require_attn_gym` can use `kernel._error` directly, and the `cast` import goes away.

#### 5. Every subclass has the same name (nit)
`type("_MissingKernel", ...)` gives each per-module subclass the same `__name__` / `__qualname__` as the base, so reprs and tracebacks can't tell them apart. Something like `f"_MissingKernel[{module_name}]"`, or a name that includes `error.name`, would make debugging easier. It costs nothing, since identity checks are gone.

#### 6. Small points (fine as they are)
- `_raise_for(None)` falling back to "first recorded backend error" is now only reachable through the zero-argument `require_attn_gym()`. The base `_MissingKernel` is only handed out when `attn_gym` is absent, and in that case `_BACKEND_ERRORS` is empty. If you drop the coarse branch (#3), this fallback can go too.
- `_BACKEND_ERRORS.setdefault` combined with the cached subclass means a second export from the same failed module reuses the first error. That is the correct behaviour.
- The tests are thorough. The mixed triton/cutlass case in a single process covers the original bug directly.

Thanks @tianyu-l for the review. Pushed a follow up commit addressing it:

1. `ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` now check the exports they call in `__init__` (`context_parallel_kda` / `context_parallel_gdn`, `context_parallel_conv_history`, `ContextParallelRouting`, plus `l2norm` for GDN), and `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN` check `causal_conv1d`, so every module keeps the fails at build contract. New `test_attention_modules_report_their_own_backend_at_build` covers both directions, with the CP modules broken the inner modules build and the CP ones fail with the CP backend, with `short_conv` broken the kernels build and the inner modules fail. It fails on the previous revision. `InnerGDN` only needs `causal_conv1d` on its packed sequence and CP paths (the no cu_seqlens path is pure torch), I kept one rule, check every export the module can call, rather than special casing that path, happy to narrow it if you prefer. The `causal_conv1d` checks only bite once the lazy export follow up lands, today a missing cutlass fails at import of `kda.py` / `gdn.py`, as the description notes.
2. Every `require_attn_gym` call has a keep in sync comment.

### Re-review after f51e271

I have no blocking comments. All five points from the first review are addressed, and the new commit reads cleanly.

#### Earlier points
| # | Point | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CP failures surfaced only at `forward` | ✅ `ContextParallelInnerKDA` / `ContextParallelInnerGDN` check their exports in `__init__`, and `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN` check `causal_conv1d`. MRO is fine: `CPInnerAttention` has no `__init__`, so `super().__init__(config)` reaches `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN.__init__`, which then builds the kernel. All three layers are checked, outermost first. |
| 2 | Kernel lists can drift from `forward` | ✅ Each call has a keep-in-sync comment |
| 3 | Zero-argument coarse form | ✅ Removed. The signature `require_attn_gym(kernel, *kernels)` makes an empty call a `TypeError` |
| 4 | `TypeGuard` | ✅ No `cast` remains |
| 5 | Placeholder names | ✅ Placeholders are named `_MissingKernel[<module>]` |

#### Checks on the lists against actual call sites
- `KDAKernel`: `chunk_kda` (forward), plus `bound_gate` and `l2norm` (`prepare_inputs`). Complete.
- `GDNKernel`: `chunk_gdn` and `l2norm` (forward), and `recurrent_gdn` (inside `_recurrent_gdn_fwd`). Complete.
- `InnerKDA` / `InnerGDN`: `causal_conv1d`, also reached through `_causal_conv1d_varlen`. Complete. Applying the rule uniformly, including the pure-torch no-`cu_seqlens` path in GDN, seems right to me. A model that can only build in some layouts would be surprising.
- `ContextParallelInnerKDA`: `context_parallel_conv_history` (`short_convolution`), `context_parallel_kda` (`kda_core`), and `ContextParallelRouting` (via `prepare_linear_attention_cp_metadata`, which calls `ContextParallelRouting.from_fragments`). Complete.
- `ContextParallelInnerGDN`: the same exports plus `l2norm` in `gdn_core`. Complete.
- When `attn_gym` is not installed, the old `_load_module("attn_gym") is None` branch is no longer needed. Every export then resolves to the base `_MissingKernel` with `_error = None`, so `require_attn_gym` still raises the install hint.
- No `is _MissingKernel` / `is not _MissingKernel` identity checks remain outside tests.

#### Remaining nits (optional)
1. **The CP case in the new test can't catch a dropped export.** In the `context_parallel` parametrization, all three CP modules fail with the same backend (`triton`). Removing, say, `context_parallel_conv_history` or `ContextParallelRouting` from the `cp_kda.py` list would still pass, because `context_parallel_kda` raises `triton` first. To make each entry load-bearing, break one module per case and give each its own backend name. For example: `attn_gym.linear.context_parallel` → `"backend_a"` should fail both CP modules, and `attn_gym.linear.kda.context_parallel` → `"backend_b"` should fail only `cp_inner_kda`. This is the test-side half of point 2: the comment documents the contract, and this would enforce it.
   [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20attn-gym-per-kernel-errors%2C%20in%20tests%2Funit_tests%2Fcpu%2Fmodels%2Fcommon%2Ftest_optional_imports.py%20test_attention_modules_report_their_own_backend_at_build%2C%20split%20the%20context_parallel%20parametrization%20so%20each%20of%20attn_gym.linear.context_parallel%2C%20attn_gym.linear.kda.context_parallel%20and%20attn_gym.linear.gdn.context_parallel%20is%20broken%20on%20its%20own%20(with%20a%20distinct%20backend%20name)%2C%20asserting%20exactly%20which%20of%20cp_inner_kda%20%2F%20cp_inner_gdn%20fail%20with%20that%20backend%20and%20that%20the%20others%20build.&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)
2. **The vLLM inner modules still fail late (out of scope, pre-existing).** `VLLMInnerKDA` and `VLLMInnerGDN` (`torchtitan/rl/generator/vllm/{kda,gdn}.py`) call `paged_chunk_kda`, `paged_causal_conv1d`, `causal_conv1d_decode`, `recurrent_*_decode`, `l2norm` and `bound_gate`, but never call `require_attn_gym`. A missing backend therefore only shows up at the first generator step. They never had the check, so this PR doesn't regress them. It could go into the lazy-`short_conv` follow-up if you want the build-time guarantee to cover the generator too.
